discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 031723
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
Issued by National Weather Service Grand Rapids MI
1223 PM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Breezy and dry today with record-challenging warmth. Southerly
  wind gusts of 25 mph to perhaps 35 mph. 

- Rain arrives from west to east late tonight. Breezy with
  lingering showers through Wednesday.

- Not as warm to end the week with lake enhanced showers at
  times.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 249 AM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

A well defined upper-level trough is lifting north-northeast through 
Kansas early this morning. Closer to home, low stratus and patchy 
drizzle continues to lift north through Michigan in response to this 
lifting cyclone. Stout warm air advection has brought steadily 
rising temperatures on this shift with an increasing number of 60-
degree readings (normal high today is only 55). That said, morning 
temperatures will be a nice spring board for afternoon highs that 
will challenge the day's records: 76 degrees in 2003 and 1987 (2003 
record was only at Fort Wayne). Rather cloudy immediately upstream, 
but clearing is noted across the Ohio River. This could be enough 
later today to truly challenge the record. Cloud cover will also 
dictate afternoon mixing of the low-level jet. Forecast soundings 
depict a narrow window after 1pm where guidance attempts to mix down 
35 mph gusts. Overall today, breezy, decreasing clouds (especially 
along and east of the I-69 corridor) and dry. 

Rain slowly arrives from west to east Tuesday night according to 
available near-term models (RIP HREF, NAM et. al.). Northwest Ohio 
could very well be dry until after daybreak Wednesday as low 
pressure becomes stacked beneath the parent upper-low, slowing the 
cold front's arrival. Breezy conditions persist into Wednesday 
morning as the low-level jet remains amplified over northwest Ohio. 
A dry slot from this low slowly works its way east permitting some 
afternoon dry hours. Cooler air behind this system seeps in 
Wednesday night through Thursday along with lake-enhanced showers. 
Highs in the 60s Wednesday and Thursday give way to highs in the 50s 
Friday through the weekend. This whole system exits later Saturday 
ending the lake-enhanced shower chance.

Beyond the weekend, subtle northwest flow results in temperatures 
fairly close to normal and opportunities for 20% POPs at times as 
weak disturbances ripple through the flow. Subtle ridging is noted 
over the southern and central US, which, if building into the 
Midwest could later induce a more zonal flow locally. However, the 
core global models are teasing chilly Canadian High pressure after 
Veteran's Day.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1222 PM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

Satellite shows earlier widespread stratus has cleared the
terminals with FEW to SCT clouds expected through the evening in
the 3-6kft range. Clouds increase in coverage overnight with the
approach of a cold front, with a few hours of LLWS favored ahead
of the front as winds near 2kft approach 45 knots. This front
will also bring rain showers after 09z continuing through the
end of the TAF period. The combination of showers and increasing
low-level moisture will cause conditions to deteriorate to MVFR,
with cigs possibly falling below 2kft after 14z (best chance at
FWA). In addition, south to south-southeast winds will be 
gusting to 25 knots throughout the forecast period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 AM EST Wednesday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Thomas

spc.text:
SPC AC 031626

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1026 AM CST Tue Nov 03 2026

   Valid 031630Z - 041200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM EAST TEXAS
   NORTH AND EAST INTO THE LOWER AND MID-MISSISSIPPI VALLEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with potential for isolated severe wind gusts and
   perhaps a brief tornado or two will be possible today from the
   Sabine and Lower Mississippi Valleys northward into the Mid
   Mississippi Valley.

   ... Synopsis ...

   A midlevel cyclone over the southern Plains this morning will
   continue to slowly deepen today as it lifts northeast toward the
   upper Midwest. An associated surface cyclone over northeast Kansas
   this morning will lift northeast into eastern Iowa during the day
   before pivoting north then northwestward overnight as it occludes.
   At the same time, an attendant surface baroclinic zone will push
   east across the southern Plains today, with an appreciable moist
   plume on the east side of the baroclinic zone.

   Morning water vapor imagery shows a pronounced shortwave trough
   entering the basal region of the longer-wave trough in which the
   midlevel cyclone resides. As this shortwave trough exits the basal
   region later today, it will take on an increasingly negative tilt
   and southerly midlevel flow above the Lower and Mid-Mississippi
   valleys will be sustained. In response to the evolving mid- and
   upper-level kinematic fields, the low-level jet will be sustained
   and move northeast, tied to the progress of the negatively tilted
   trough.


   ... East Texas toward the Lower Mississippi Valley ...

   Thunderstorms are ongoing this morning within the broad moist plume
   ahead of the aforementioned baroclinic zone. Within this moist
   plume, weak midlevel lapse rates and a modest low-level theta-e
   airmass has held instability in check today -- generally less than
   1000 J/kg. Given low-level moisture trajectories, widespread cloud
   cover ahead of the advancing baroclinic zone, and weak lapse rates
   upstream of the region, instability should not really recover much
   today. 

   That said, low-level and large-scale forcing for ascent will
   continue to support convection through the afternoon and into the
   overnight hours. The strength of the kinematic fields will yield
   some tornado/wind potential within the various convective bands --
   especially where any low-level instability can develop.
   Additionally, transient supercell or supercell-like thunderstorms
   may develop ahead of the line within the broad warm-air advection
   regime. These shallow, but rotating, thunderstorms will also pose at
   least some potential for tornado/wind damage as well. 

   This threat should continue into the overnight hours across portions
   of western Tennessee and western Kentucky, especially if a zone of
   more discrete showers/thunderstorms can develop within the nocturnal
   low-level jet.


   ... Mid-Mississippi Valley ...

   As the surface-low deepens this afternoon and evening, strong
   low-level wind fields will be maintained or even strengthen,
   yielding ESRH on the order of 250-350 m2/s2. As strong southerly
   midlevel flow is sustained in response to the approaching midlevel
   shortwave trough, effective-layer shear in excess of 50 knots will
   be maintained or overspread much of the region. This far north,
   instability will be even more limited than compared to areas farther
   south. However, convergence along the surface front and large-scale
   ascent from the midlevel wave will support bands of forced
   convection during the day and into the evening. The strong kinematic
   fields may be sufficient to offset the meager buoyancy and support a
   potential for isolated tornado/wind damage.

   ..Marsh/Supinie.. 11/03/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 031716

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1116 AM CST Tue Nov 03 2026

   Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.

   ...Southeast States...
   A broad upper trough will continue to move slowly eastward across
   the central/eastern states on Wednesday, with a potent shortwave
   trough affecting the southern Appalachians.  Thunderstorms will
   likely be ongoing at 12z Wednesday morning over middle TN and
   northern AL, with activity persisting and moving eastward into parts
   of east TN/GA/western Carolinas through the afternoon.  Strong flow
   aloft may result in localized damaging wind gusts, but instability
   will be very weak.  A small 5% wind area was considered for
   northeast AL/northwest GA, but given the weak CAPE fields will defer
   to later updates.

   ..Hart.. 11/03/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 030810

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0210 AM CST Tue Nov 03 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A shortwave trough will move across the central Plains and into the
   MS Valley where it will phase with the trough extending southward
   across the Great Lakes. This combined positive-tilt trough will then
   sweep eastward toward the OH and TN valleys overnight.

   Well ahead of this trough, southerly winds will bring 60s F
   dewpoints northward across the Mid Atlantic, though instability will
   be relatively weak. Isolated daytime convection may occur from GA
   into the Carolinas, but lapse rates and shear will both be poor.
   Scattered showers may persist overnight as a weak surface trough
   develops and southwest low-level winds maintain a moist air mass.

   ..Jewell.. 11/03/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
